items.headline: Anthropic reports $17B Q3 revenue ahead of IPO
items.summary: Anthropic released an amended IPO prospectus showing roughly $17 billion in third-quarter revenue alongside a net loss of $23.29 billion. The disclosures bring the Claude maker closer to one of the largest IPOs in history, though some investors are weighing a lower valuation.

items.headline: Anthropic's quarterly loss shrinks as revenue jumps
items.summary: Reuters reported Anthropic's quarterly loss narrowed and revenue surged ahead of its planned blockbuster IPO. The company is expected to begin marketing shares to investors the week of November 9.

items.headline: OpenAI deepens Abu Dhabi ties with sweeping AI deals
items.summary: OpenAI signed agreements across energy, investment, and government sectors with ADNOC, G42, Mubadala, and the Abu Dhabi Government. The deals extend OpenAI's reach into the UAE as it taps Middle East investors for ever-larger pools of capital.

items.headline: OpenAI cuts funding round to $20B at $1.25T valuation
items.summary: OpenAI trimmed its new funding round target to about $20 billion at a valuation near $1.25 trillion, according to the FT. UAE investors including MGX are pairing capital with compute capacity in the raise.

items.headline: Marvell to buy Lumentum in all-stock AI connectivity deal
items.summary: Marvell announced it will acquire Lumentum in an all-stock deal, combining electrical and optical technologies to meet accelerating AI connectivity demands. Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.5 Marvell shares per share, with the deal expected to close in the first half of 2028.

items.headline: Oracle to raise $20B to fund AI infrastructure build-out
items.summary: Oracle plans to raise $20 billion through bond and share sales, regulatory filings showed Monday. The software giant is tapping investors to finance its costly AI and cloud infrastructure expansion.

items.headline: OpenAI launches Grid Protectors Program for compute campuses
items.summary: OpenAI introduced a national program to help its future compute campuses support reliable, affordable electricity. The initiative addresses growing concerns about AI data centers' strain on the power grid.

items.headline: BofA warns AI boom is a major risk to global economy
items.summary: BofA Global Research cautioned about the sustainability of the AI trade the day before a midterm vote framed around data-center backlash. The warning highlights mounting concerns over the AI trade's impact on the broader economy.

items.headline: Howard Marks says AI stumbles have boosted skepticism
items.summary: Oaktree's Howard Marks told Bloomberg TV that recent AI-related market stumbles have burst the sector's aura of infallibility. His comments reflect growing investor doubts about the sustainability of the AI boom.

items.headline: Anthropic warns its AI could pose existential risks
items.summary: Anthropic's owners warned that its technology could pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity without appropriate safeguards. The dire self-assessment comes as the company prepares for a record-breaking IPO, raising questions about investor appetite.

items.headline: Germany urges faster push to preserve AI sovereignty
items.summary: Chancellor Merz said Germany and Europe must move more quickly to develop their own AI capabilities to protect their digital sovereignty. The remarks signal rising European concern over dependence on US AI providers.

items.headline: Syndigo partners with Microsoft on AI commerce solutions
items.summary: Syndigo announced a multi-year partnership with Microsoft to develop AI-powered commerce solutions integrating Microsoft Foundry and Agent 365. The products will be co-sold through Microsoft's global sales organization.

items.headline: Investors game out midterms' impact on AI spending
items.summary: Reuters reported that the November 3 US midterm results could heighten investor concerns about AI spending and debt ceiling negotiations. The contests are framed partly around a growing data-center backlash.

items.headline: China's robot makers race to master AI 'brains'
items.summary: Chinese embodied AI companies raised 93.5 billion yuan ($13 billion) across 322 deals in the first half of 2026, five times the prior year. As hardware prices fall, funding is shifting toward specialist developers of robot intelligence.

items.headline: White House task force to report on AI risks in 120 days
items.summary: A new White House task force will have 120 days to report on AI risks and opportunities and define the federal government's responsibility. DNI Jay Clayton effectively becomes the administration's AI czar, focused on US leadership in superintelligence.

items.headline: AI talent war spreads to Wall Street quant firms
items.summary: Quantitative trading firms are competing with AI labs for top scientists, with first-year PhD compensation reaching as much as $800,000. Firms are using fellowships, sponsorships, and recruiting events to counter lucrative AI company offers.

items.headline: Klein and Glazer call to block reckless AI IPOs
items.summary: Naomi Klein and Ilana Glazer argued in The Guardian that it's time to block reckless AI IPOs and tax billionaires. The op-ed reflects growing public pushback against AI wealth concentration ahead of Anthropic's debut.

items.headline: Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom back Meta's $25B stock sale
items.summary: The chip makers acted as $5 billion cornerstone investors in Meta's $25 billion stock sale, highlighting the circular financing underpinning AI. The move came just before rising concerns over AI infrastructure financing hit tech stocks hard.

items.headline: Big Tech AI capex set to reach $828B this year
items.summary: Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta, and SpaceX/xAI are collectively on track to spend as much as $828 billion on capital expenditures in 2026. The spending covers data centers, chips, and infrastructure fueling the AI boom.

items.headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Argon for hardest problems
items.summary: Google introduced Gemini 4 Argon, a model built to tackle complex tasks across engineering, legal, finance, science, and cybersecurity. Priced at $4 per 1M input and $20 per 1M output tokens after an introductory period ending November 30.
